claims.text: The initial material is a nanocrystalline CuMoTaWV refractory high-entropy alloy film.
The CuMoTaWV film is prepared by single-target magnetron sputtering.
A multilayer or functionally graded coating can tailor the top interface to produce controlled oxidation or nitride formation during operation.
The coated CuMoTaWV film is intended to operate from room temperature to at least 300 °C and potentially up to higher temperatures under extreme load and thermal cycling.
The coating will foster in situ formation of an adaptive, stable, lubricious oxide or nitride tribofilm at elevated temperatures.
The tribofilm will remain bound to the underlying CuMoTaWV alloy.
Gradual compositional and structural variation in the engineered coating promotes development of the tribofilm.
The resulting tribofilm reduces friction during high-temperature exposure.
The engineered coating and tribofilm preserve the mechanical integrity of the underlying RHEA during high-temperature exposure.
The underlying CuMoTaWV RHEA has high mechanical strength at elevated temperature.
The multilayer-coated alloy will have a lower friction coefficient than the unmodified film across an extended temperature range.
The multilayer-coated alloy will have greater wear resistance than the unmodified film across an extended temperature range.
The multilayer-coated alloy will maintain high hardness and strength during wide-temperature operation.
The unmodified nanocrystalline CuMoTaWV film has demonstrated effective performance up to 300 °C.
The unmodified CuMoTaWV film has limited self-lubrication and wear resistance above 300 °C.
Tribological performance may decline if the tribofilm or coating interface degrades at extremely high temperature or under long-term thermal cycling.
